nodes.title: Initiate Payment
nodes.summary: This API allows initiating transactions by making server calls that return a checkout URL for the payment modal.

nodes.title: Enter Payment details
nodes.summary: This section guides users on providing payment details for initiating transactions.

nodes.title: Initiate Transaction
nodes.summary: This endpoint initiates a transaction by making server calls and returns a checkout URL.

nodes.title: cURL Example (Initiate Transaction)
nodes.summary: A cURL example demonstrating how to call the transaction initiation endpoint with required headers and raw data.

nodes.title: Parameters
nodes.summary: This section lists all the required and optional parameters for the transaction initiation endpoint, including headers and body fields.

nodes.title: Header Parameters
nodes.summary: Describes the 'Authorization' header parameter for authenticating transaction initiation requests using API keys.

nodes.title: Body Parameters
nodes.summary: Describes body parameters like email, amount, currency, transaction reference, and other details for the transaction initiation request.

nodes.title: Responses
nodes.summary: This section outlines the possible HTTP responses and their structures for the transaction initiation endpoint.

nodes.title: 200 OK Response
nodes.summary: Details the successful response (HTTP 200 OK) for the transaction initiation, including data like checkout URL, transaction reference, and merchant information.

nodes.title: 401 Unauthorized Response
nodes.summary: Details the unauthorized response (HTTP 401) for the transaction initiation, indicating invalid or missing authorization keys.

nodes.title: 400 Bad Request Response
nodes.summary: Details the bad request response (HTTP 400) for the transaction initiation, often due to missing required parameters like 'email'.

nodes.title: Sample Request (Initiate Payment)
nodes.summary: Provides a sample JSON payload for initiating a payment request, including amount, email, currency, and callback URL.

nodes.title: Simulate Test Payment (Transfer)
nodes.summary: This section explains how to simulate a payment into a dynamic virtual account in the test environment to complete a transaction.

nodes.title: Simulate Payment
nodes.summary: This endpoint allows simulating a payment into a dynamically generated virtual account.

nodes.title: Parameters
nodes.summary: Lists the header and body parameters required for simulating a payment into a virtual account.

nodes.title: Header Parameters
nodes.summary: Describes the 'Authorization' header parameter for authenticating simulate payment requests.

nodes.title: Body Parameters
nodes.summary: Describes body parameters like 'virtual_account_number' and 'amount' for simulating a payment.

nodes.title: Responses
nodes.summary: Outlines the possible HTTP responses and their structures for the simulate payment endpoint.

nodes.title: 200 OK Response
nodes.summary: Details the successful response (HTTP 200 OK) for simulating a payment, confirming 'Payment successful'.

nodes.title: 400 Bad Request Response
nodes.summary: Details the bad request response (HTTP 400) for simulating a payment, typically due to missing required fields like 'amount'.

nodes.title: Sample Request (Simulate Payment)
nodes.summary: Provides a sample JSON payload for simulating a payment into a virtual account with a specified amount.

nodes.title: Recurring Payment (Charge Authorization on Card)
nodes.summary: This section describes how to set up and manage recurring payments by charging an authorized card without collecting card information each time.

nodes.title: Card Tokenization
nodes.summary: Explains how the system uses card tokenization for security and future transactions, requiring an 'is_recurring' flag in the initiate payload.

nodes.title: Sample Request (Card Tokenization)
nodes.summary: Provides a sample JSON payload for initiating a payment with card tokenization enabled by setting 'is_recurring' to true.

nodes.title: Sample Webhook Response (Tokenized Card)
nodes.summary: Illustrates a sample webhook response confirming a successful charge and providing the `token_id` for a tokenized card.

nodes.title: Charge Card
nodes.summary: This section details how to charge a card using a previously obtained `token_id` for subsequent transactions.

nodes.title: Charge Card (with Token)
nodes.summary: This endpoint debits a credit card using a token_id acquired from a previous tokenized transaction.

nodes.title: Parameters
nodes.summary: Lists the body parameters required for charging a card with a token, including amount and token_id.

nodes.title: Body Parameters
nodes.summary: Describes body parameters like 'amount', 'token_id', and 'transaction_ref' for charging a card using its token.

nodes.title: Responses
nodes.summary: Outlines the possible HTTP responses and their structures for the charge card endpoint.

nodes.title: 200 OK Response
nodes.summary: Details the successful response (HTTP 200 OK) for charging a card with a token, including transaction details.

nodes.title: 400 Bad Request Response
nodes.summary: Details the bad request response (HTTP 400) for charging a card, often due to an invalid or missing 'amount'.

nodes.title: Sample Request (Charge Card)
nodes.summary: Provides a sample JSON payload for charging a card using its token_id and a specified amount.

nodes.title: Cancel Charge Card
nodes.summary: This endpoint allows canceling a previously tokenized card, thereby revoking its authorization for future recurring charges.

nodes.title: Cancel Recurring Token
nodes.summary: This endpoint cancels active tokens to prevent further recurring charges on a card.

nodes.title: Parameters
nodes.summary: Lists the body parameters required for canceling a recurring payment token.

nodes.title: Body Parameters
nodes.summary: Describes the 'auth_code' body parameter, which is the token ID sent via webhook at the first tokenized call.

nodes.title: Responses
nodes.summary: Outlines the possible HTTP responses and their structures for the cancel recurring token endpoint.

nodes.title: 200 OK Response
nodes.summary: Details the successful response (HTTP 200 OK) for canceling a recurring payment token, listing the revoked auth_code.

nodes.title: 400 Bad Request Response
nodes.summary: Details the bad request response (HTTP 400) for canceling a recurring payment, indicating that the cancellation failed.

nodes.title: Sample Request (Cancel Recurring)
nodes.summary: Provides a sample JSON payload for canceling a recurring card token using an array of auth_codes.

nodes.title: Query All Transactions
nodes.summary: This endpoint allows querying all transactions and filtering them using multiple parameters like transaction reference, dates, and amount.

nodes.title: Query Transactions
nodes.summary: This endpoint retrieves a list of all transactions, allowing filtering by currency, start and end dates, page, perpage, and reference.

nodes.title: Parameters
nodes.summary: Lists the query parameters required for filtering and retrieving transactions, including date ranges, currency, and pagination.

nodes.title: Query Parameters
nodes.summary: Describes query parameters such as currency, start_date, end_date, page, perpage, and reference for transaction queries.

nodes.title: Responses
nodes.summary: Outlines the possible HTTP responses and their structures for the query transactions endpoint.

nodes.title: 200 OK Response
nodes.summary: Details the successful response (HTTP 200 OK) for querying transactions, returning an array of detailed transaction objects.

nodes.title: 400 Bad Request Response
nodes.summary: Details the bad request response (HTTP 400) for querying transactions, often due to missing or invalid date parameters.

nodes.title: Go Live
nodes.summary: Provides instructions on how to transition from the sandbox environment to the live production environment, including URL changes and API key usage.
